svg.title: Limen connection sequence
svg.desc: Sequence of a Limen session: login and certificate, authorization and session grant, routing over the worker tunnel, per-session credentials, and audit.

text.tspan: What happens when you run limen ssh prod-db
One login, one connection, one audit trail. Every credential in the path is short-lived and every step is checked twice
You prove who you are and get a certificate that expires in 10 minutes
Policy is checked at the proxy and again at the worker; the worker connects to the target
Everything that happened becomes an audit event before the session is allowed to continue
OIDC authorization code with PKCE (or device code)
its nonce is bound to the public keys your CLI just generated
the proxy relays it, and cannot swap in its own keys
Verify token, map IdP groups to roles,
sign with the CA key in KMS
SessionRequest: resource, login or DB role
Yes: sign a 60-second session grant, audit session.start
Stream over the worker's outbound tunnel
with the signed grant (via a peer proxy if needed)
Own policy copy allows too? (both must)
Connects with a credential made for this session
SSH certificate (1 min) · IAM token · kube impersonation
Your session: end-to-end through the proxy and worker, which the worker records
Commands, queries and the recording, as audit events
spooled to disk first, then relayed through the proxy
Append to the hash chain, write batches to S3
If audit cannot be written: no new sessions
Certificate 10 min, session grant 60 s, SSH certificate 1 min,
IAM token for the connect only. A stolen credential is
The proxy and the worker each evaluate policy from signed
snapshots. A compromised proxy cannot reach a target
the worker's policy does not allow.
No audit, no session. If the control plane or KMS is down,
new SSH and logins stop, and database or Kubernetes access
continues only within a 5-minute policy grace period.
